scheme_name: National Mission For Sustainable Agriculture-Parmparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (NMSA-PKVY)
description:
The National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture-Parmparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (NMSA-PKVY) is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India in 2015. 

This scheme is part of the larger National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture. 

The primary objective of the NMSA-PKVY is to promote organic farming in India. 

The scheme aims to enhance the income of farmers through sustainable agricultural practices. 

It encourages the adoption of organic farming techniques to improve soil health and reduce chemical inputs. 

The NMSA-PKVY focuses on promoting traditional farming methods that are environmentally friendly. 

The mission also aims to increase the area under organic farming to 2 million hectares by 2025. 

The government has set a target to train 1 million farmers in organic farming practices by 2025. 

The benefits of the NMSA-PKVY include financial assistance for farmers transitioning to organic farming. 

Farmers can receive up to ₹50,000 per hectare for three years under this scheme. 

This financial assistance is provided to cover the costs of organic inputs and certification. 

The scheme also facilitates the establishment of organic farming clusters. 

These clusters are designed to promote collective farming and marketing of organic produce. 

The NMSA-PKVY provides support for the development of organic value chains. 

This includes assistance for processing and marketing organic products. 

Eligibility for the NMSA-PKVY is primarily targeted at farmers engaged in agriculture. 

Farmers must be willing to adopt organic farming practices. 

There are no specific age limits for eligibility under this scheme. 

However, farmers must have a valid landholding to qualify for assistance. 

The income criteria are not strictly defined but preference is given to small and marginal farmers. 

To apply for the NMSA-PKVY, farmers must follow a specific process. 

The first step is to approach the local agricultural department or Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK). 

Farmers need to fill out an application form available at these centers. 

Required documents include proof of land ownership and identity proof. 

Farmers must also submit a project proposal outlining their organic farming plans. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the concerned authorities. 

The approval process typically takes 30 to 45 days. 

Upon approval, farmers will receive financial assistance directly into their bank accounts. 

The disbursement of funds is usually done in installments based on the progress of the project. 

The NMSA-PKVY is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The National Centre of Organic Farming is the nodal agency for this scheme. 

State governments also play a crucial role in the implementation of the NMSA-PKVY. 

They are responsible for monitoring and evaluating the progress of the scheme at the state level. 

The scheme has seen significant participation from various states. 

States like Sikkim have been pioneers in organic farming and have benefited from the NMSA-PKVY. 

The scheme also promotes the use of organic fertilizers and bio-pesticides. 

Farmers are encouraged to utilize locally available resources for organic farming. 

The NMSA-PKVY has provisions for capacity building and training programs. 

These programs are conducted by agricultural universities and research institutions. 

Farmers are trained in various aspects of organic farming including pest management and soil health. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of certification for organic produce. 

Farmers are guided on how to obtain organic certification from accredited agencies. 

The NMSA-PKVY has provisions for creating awareness about organic farming. 

Awareness campaigns are conducted to educate farmers about the benefits of organic farming. 

The scheme also aims to promote organic farming as a viable livelihood option. 

The NMSA-PKVY has been instrumental in increasing the area under organic farming in India. 

As of 2023, India has over 3 million hectares of land under organic cultivation. 

The government aims to increase this area significantly in the coming years. 

The NMSA-PKVY has also contributed to the growth of the organic market in India. 

The demand for organic products has been rising steadily in both domestic and international markets. 

Farmers participating in the scheme have reported increased incomes due to higher prices for organic produce. 

The NMSA-PKVY also encourages the use of traditional seeds and indigenous crops. 

This helps in conserving biodiversity and promoting sustainable agriculture. 

The scheme has provisions for research and development in organic farming practices. 

The government collaborates with various research institutions to promote innovative practices. 

The NMSA-PKVY is aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) set by the United Nations. 

It aims to promote sustainable agriculture and ensure food security. 

The scheme also addresses issues related to climate change and environmental sustainability. 

Farmers are encouraged to adopt practices that mitigate the effects of climate change. 

The NMSA-PKVY has received positive feedback from farmers across the country. 

Many farmers have reported improved soil health and increased crop yields. 

The scheme has also fostered a sense of community among organic farmers. 

Farmers are encouraged to form cooperatives for better marketing of their produce. 

The NMSA-PKVY has been a step towards making agriculture more sustainable in India. 

It has empowered farmers to take control of their farming practices. 

The scheme has also played a crucial role in promoting health and nutrition. 

Organic farming practices contribute to the production of healthier food. 

The NMSA-PKVY is a comprehensive initiative aimed at transforming Indian agriculture. 

It provides a framework for sustainable farming practices that benefit both farmers and consumers. 

The government continues to promote the NMSA-PKVY through various outreach programs. 

Overall, the NMSA-PKVY represents a significant shift towards sustainable agriculture in India. 

It is a vital component of the government's efforts to enhance the livelihoods of farmers. 

The scheme is expected to evolve further with changing agricultural practices and market demands.
